ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0; AntiMoney Laundering Ordinance (AMLO/GwV) of 11 November 2015, SR 955.01; Swiss Criminal Code arts. 305bis and 305ter, SR 311.0; Code of Obligations arts. 626, 640, and 697i697m (share register and bearer share UBO duty), SR 220; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV/ORC) of 17 October 2007, SR 221.411; Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions (Embargo Act) of 22 March 2002, SR 946.231.11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's country of domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) or Swiss consular legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Declaration identifying all natural persons owning 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Swiss incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the principal's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by notary + Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; original bank confirmation with SWIFT reference for blocked account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and commercial counterparties against the SECO consolidated sanctions list (UN and autonomous Swiss measures), FINMA enforcement notices, EU restrictive measures adopted by Switzerland, and OFAC SDN list including the 50% ownership rule for all USD-denominated Swift wires; PEP screening must be performed through an automated database (e.g., World-Check or equivalent) with substantive risk review and a complete audit trail retained for at least 10 years per AMLA record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix, zefix.ch) operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office; formal filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm name must use Latin script and be expressed in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh); for a Zug-domiciled AG the preferred form is German, e.g., 'Hazy IPA Distribution AG'; the legal-form suffix must be 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the permitted abbreviation 'AG'; the name must be truthful and not deceptive under Art. 954 of the Code of Obligations and the Federal Ordinance on Company Names (Firmenverordnung), must not imply a different business scope, and foreign script is not permitted in the registered name; foreign-origin brand tokens must be transliterated into Latin characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Sparkasse, Banque (requires FINMA banking license)
Versicherung, Assurance, Insurance (requires FINMA insurance license)
Trust, Fiduciary, Revisions, Audit (requires professional licensing or creates deceptive impression)
Swiss, Schweiz, Suisse, Svizzera, Helvetia (requires administrative authorization to protect geographical designation)
Holding (requires real holding substance and parent company guarantee)
Beer, Brauerei, Brewery (requires alignment with the Federal Beer Act licensing and excise registration to avoid deception)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 days of receipt of the rejection notice, submit a written administrative appeal to the Cantonal Appeal Commission for Commercial Register Matters (Verwaltungsgericht des Kantons Zug), attaching the preliminary clearance decision and an amended or clarified business-scope statement; if the cantonal appeal is dismissed, file a public-law appeal with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht, Lausanne) within 30 days; alternatively, reserve a different name and revert to the contested token only after obtaining the specific ministerial or licensing authority's written consent; the initial non-binding preliminary name check is free of charge, while the formal registration docket fee covers the appeal filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only for the registered seat if the address is a physical Swiss business office where process service, commercial register correspondence, and tax correspondence can be actually received and acknowledged; a pure letterbox in a business center is tolerated solely for the headquarters element; however, the cold-chain wholesale distribution operation requires a physically manifest licensed storage or dispatch facility, or a contractual third-party logistics (TPL) cold-chain warehouse with a declared address to the Federal Customs Administration and the Cantonal Food Control Authority; therefore, a virtual office alone is impermissible for the licensed craft beer distribution activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by customs excise officers, cantonal food control (Lebensmittelkontrolle), or alcohol-regime inspectors within the first 24 months of operation, driven by cold-chain integrity checks, excise bookkeeping verification, and beer import documentation under the Federal Customs Administration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht) Arts. 620–659b and 626–635 (incorporation of Aktiengesellschaft); Art. 632 (minimum paid-up capital); Art. 640 (registration in Commercial Register); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV); cantonal notarization law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office, with notification to the federal Central Business Names Index (Zefix).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially executed deed of incorporation and articles of association (Statuten), filed electronically through the Commercial Register application platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an AG is CHF 100,000; before registration at least 20% of each cash share, and at least CHF 50,000 in aggregate, must be paid up and secured through a Swiss bank blocked-account confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) or a cantonal public deposit; contributions in kind must be fully paid up and independently audited if required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned directors, constituting the first Board of the company, ratify the subscription and issuance of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100.00 each, representing CHF 100,000 share capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at Bahnhofstrasse 10, CH-8001 Zurich, with service of process accepted at that address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Company Secretary, and [Name] Anti-Money Laundering Officer, each with sole signature for ordinary operations and joint signature for registration acts, effective immediately upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and notarial execution of the deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) acting on instruction of a licensed Swiss notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Central Business Names Index (Zefix) for name conflicts, reserve a unique name containing the legal suffix AG, prepare the draft statutes and subscription lists, and execute the incorporation deed before a notary; the notary registers the name reservation and submits the public deed to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or ID of each founder
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register objects to the name or deed, amend the distinctive part of the company name or supplement the notarial attestation within the official ten-day curing period and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked share capital deposit and bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank providing a blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account at a Swiss bank in the company's name, transfer the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (or 100% of the subscribed capital), and obtain a Sperrbestätigung addressed to the Commercial Register confirming the amount is at the bank's free disposal restriction and available to the company after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue a blocked-account confirmation, apply to another licensed bank or deposit the funds with the cantonal public treasury and use that receipt as equivalent proof of payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the certified deed, statutes, blocked-account confirmation, and board acceptance declarations via the official Commercial Register web portal; the registrar reviews legal compliance, assigns the UID number, and issues the official excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug).
required_dossiers: Written declaration of board members accepting office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the noted deficiencies by supplemental filing; if the registry maintains refusal, appeal to the Cantonal Commercial Register Court within the statutory notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, AHV and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Office, and Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the federal business start-up portal after obtaining the Commercial Register excerpt to register for corporate income tax, VAT (MWST) where turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, AHV/IV/EO employer contributions, and withholding tax; obtain the VAT number and AHV employer number before hiring staff.
required_dossiers: Identification of directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file late registrations proactively with the competent tax authority and request a VAT registration reminder or use the voluntary disclosure mechanism to avoid penalty assessments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, alcohol, food safety and environmental licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Alcohol and Food Safety Inspectorate, Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO), and Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete licensing dossier prior to commencement of brewery production and distribution; include site plans, HACCP concept, wastewater and emission descriptions, alcohol permit application, and fire-safety documents; obtain final operating certificate and EIA registration confirmation.
required_dossiers: Detailed floor plan of production and storage areas
HACCP plan and food safety self-monitoring concept
Wastewater discharge and air emission description
Fire safety concept and occupational certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a defect notice, provide supplementary technical evidence within the deadline; a negative decision may be administratively reviewed by the Cantonal Administrative Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Alcohol and Commerce Office (Gewerbeamt), Federal Alcohol Authority (Eidgenössische Alkoholverwaltung, EAV), and Federal Customs Administration for beer excise duty (Generalzolldirektion)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal alcohol trade/manufacturing permit and Food Business Operator registration (Lebensmittelbetrieb); beer excise warehouse or trader permit under the Beer Excise Act (Biersteuergesetz) for distribution and export

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the responsible Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B registration with simplified environmental examination; full EIA report (Umweltverträglichkeitsbericht) is required only where annual beer production exceeds 20,000 hl or the installation is located in a sensitive groundwater or air-shed protection area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater must be pre-treated to meet the Federal Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 2 thresholds, including COD ≤ 60 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 20 mg/L, TSS ≤ 20 mg/L, and pH 6.5–9.0 before discharge; air emissions from brewing and fermentation must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV), including total organic carbon ≤ 150 mg/m³ and suppression of odor nuisances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire-safety certification (Brandschutzabnahme), structural load inspection for fermentation tanks and storage racks, civil-defense and emergency water supply inspection where structurally applicable, and occupational health and accident insurance confirmation (Suva or licensed private insurer) under the Federal Accident Insurance Act (UVG).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), Bern; online VAT and UID registration via the FTA eService portal (www.estv.admin.ch); cantonal tax authorities responsible for direct tax registration of permanent establishments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity seeking Swiss VAT identity must: (1) appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (Art. 67 Swiss VAT Act); (2) submit FTA VAT registration form 1030 together with foreign company extract, description of Swiss supply activities, and foreign VAT/TIN; (3) upon approval obtain Swiss VAT number (MWST/TVA) and the Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID), which serves as the general business identifier. Direct tax registration is triggered by the creation of a Swiss permanent establishment and is completed with the competent cantonal tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Switzerland does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; an Aktiengesellschaft is per se a taxable entity, and OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid rules apply mandatorily without elective options.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover for businesses domiciled in Switzerland; non-domiciled suppliers generally register without threshold when making taxable supplies in Switzerland, except where B2B services are supplied exclusively to Swiss VAT-registered businesses and turnover is below CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing, API reporting, or digital stamping. E-invoices are accepted on a voluntary basis but must comply with Swiss VAT invoice content requirements; no government-run electronic invoice clearance system is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are zero-rated when the goods are physically removed from Switzerland and delivered to the foreign buyer; the exporter must hold documentary proof of export. Certain services supplied to foreign recipients qualify for zero-rating under the B2B destination principle; for microbrewery export, title transfer, transport, and foreign receipt must be documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic declaration via e-dec/TOGAL)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (CMR/Air Waybill)
Inward remittance evidence (bank account statement, SWIFT credit advice, or certified remittance certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Insufficient export proof triggers denial of zero-rating, retrospective VAT assessment, and interest. Swiss VAT Act allows assessments within 10 years; fraudulent schemes attract criminal fines up to CHF 250,000, penalties up to three times the tax evaded, seizure of assets, and publication of the judgment. Retroactive clawback is comprehensive and does not require a fixed FX repatriation deadline as Swiss law imposes no statutory repatriation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. CHF is freely traded and remittable; no restrictions exist on dividends, royalties, or loan interest repatriation. Only statistical reporting to the SNB is required for cross-border payments of CHF 125,000 or more, with no prior administrative approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no requirement to convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. Exporters retain full discretion over foreign currency balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs without a Swiss banking license. Swiss law requires any deposit-taking or payment activity to be licensed by FINMA under the Banking Act or FinIA. EU/UK EMIs cannot passport into Switzerland. A Swiss-licensed fintech company (e.g., Yapeal, Zak) is viable but limited to payment accounts without lending or interest, and is not advisable for core treasury liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Swiss banks mandate at least one director or authorized signatory to appear physically for a KYC interview (AML-FINMA identification rules). Remote onboarding is possible for non-resident directors using video identification, certified passport copies, and apostilled corporate extracts, but is bank-specific. Where physical appearance is refused, Swiss diplomatic missions or a notarial identity form (Annex II) may substitute at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership involving jurisdictions on FATF or Swiss high-risk lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Handelsregister extract, group structure org chart, UBO declaration (Form A), source-of-wealth statement, business plan, and independent banking reference from an existing Tier-1 creditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators where shipment values, frequency, or destinations do not align with payments for craft beer export.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, Swiss customs declarations (NCTS/EMDN), supplier and distributor contracts, and cold-chain temperature log data to substantiate real physical trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) detected in the distribution chain or minority shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative PEP screening reports, SECO/OFAC/EU sanctions proof, shareholder representation letters, beneficial ownership matrix, and an enhanced due-diligence file prepared by a Swiss compliance advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank account (no cash deposits) referencing the notarized capital increase resolution. Use purpose code 'NOD' (Non-Refundable Investment) or 'EQUI' (Equity Capital Return) as per SWIFT Category 400; include the Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and the receiving bank's clearing details. The bank verifies funds against the registered share capital and may require written confirmation that the payment is a capital contribution exempt from Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For beer export settlements with EU/non-EU wholesalers, use SWIFT MT103 (Banking instructions in Field 72 /REC/) for invoice payments, or Irrevocable Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600) for large orders or high-risk markets. For intra-Swiss payments, use the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) rail; for EUR-denominated supplier payments, use SEPA Credit Transfer. Supporting documents must include commercial invoice, shipping order, and insurance certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF) up to 12 months
Cross-currency interest rate swap (for matching long-term equipment financing)
OTC transactions under ISDA 2002 and Swiss FINMA EMIR margin rules; NDFs are not standard for CHF as the currency is fully convertible and liquid

stage_5.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Art. 697j–697o CO require a register of beneficial owners for bearer and registered shares; the AG verifies UBO data upon share issuance/transfer and enters new 25%+ owners; from the entry into force of the Federal Act on Transparency of Legal Entities (planned 2025/26), the UBO register must be reported electronically to the Commercial Registrar and confirmed annually; transfers of ≥ 25% direct/indirect ownership must be notified within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Verzeichnis der Mitglieder des Verwaltungsrates)
Minute Book (Protokolle der Generalversammlung und des Verwaltungsrates)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Verzeichnis der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten)

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
